title: Identity Protection and Governance

header.html: Describe Microsoft Entra ID Governance; Describe access reviews; Describe the capabilities of Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management; Describe Microsoft Entra ID Protection
the official SC-900 study guide, skills measured as of October 21, 2026

html:
1Four tools, four jobs

Tool Job in one line Question it answers
Microsoft Entra ID Governance Make sure the right people have the right access for the right time Who should have access, and for how long?
Access reviews Regularly re-check who has access and remove what is not needed Do they still need it?
Privileged Identity Management (PIM) Give privileged roles just in time, not permanently Can administrators be admins only when needed?
Microsoft Entra ID Protection Detect and respond to identity risks Is this sign-in or user risky?

2Microsoft Entra ID Governance

ID Governance manages the identity and access life cycle at scale, balancing security and productivity. It adds capabilities to Entra ID. [Verify live] for licensing.

Capability What it does
Entitlement management Bundles resources into access packages that users request, with approval and expiry
Lifecycle workflows Automates joiner, mover and leaver tasks (create, change, remove access)
Access reviews Periodically confirm or remove access
Privileged Identity Management Just-in-time, time-bound privileged access
Terms of use Require users to accept terms before access
Exam tip

. Joiner, mover, leaver = lifecycle workflows. Access packages (a bundle of access that expires) = entitlement management.

3Access reviews

An access review lets the right people confirm whether access is still needed.

Item Details
What can be reviewed Group memberships, application access, Entra and Azure roles, access packages
Reviewers Resource owners, managers, the users themselves, or selected reviewers
Frequency One time or recurring (monthly, quarterly, yearly)
Outcome Approve or deny; access can be removed automatically when the review ends
Why Fights privilege creep and stale access and supports compliance and audits

Exam tip

. "Periodically verify that group members still need access" = access review. It removes excess access; it does not detect risky sign-ins (that is ID Protection).

4Privileged Identity Management (PIM)

PIM manages, controls and monitors access to important resources: Entra roles, Azure roles and groups.

Feature Meaning
Just-in-time (JIT) access Privileges are activated only when needed
Time-bound access Roles expire after a set time
Eligible vs active Eligible = can activate the role; active = has it now
Approval Activation can require approval
MFA on activation Require MFA to activate
Justification and notifications Users give a reason; admins get alerts
Audit history and reviews Every activation is logged; access reviews of roles

PIM reduces standing privilege: an attacker who steals an eligible admin's password still cannot use the role without activation. PIM needs Entra ID P2 (or ID Governance). [Verify live]

Exam tip

. PIM = just-in-time, time-limited admin rights. The key word is eligible: the person can become admin, but is not admin all the time.

5Microsoft Entra ID Protection

ID Protection uses machine learning and Microsoft's threat data to detect identity risks, report them and automate responses. It needs Entra ID P2. [Verify live]

Risk type Meaning
User risk The account may be compromised (for example leaked credentials)
Sign-in risk This sign-in may not be the real user (for example anonymous IP address, atypical or impossible travel, unfamiliar sign-in properties, password spray)

Responses: risk-based Conditional Access policies can require MFA for risky sign-ins and a password change for risky users; admins can investigate, confirm or dismiss risks in reports.

Exam tip

. User risk = account (leaked credentials). Sign-in risk = this login (impossible travel). ID Protection detects; Conditional Access acts on the risk.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors wants administrators to be admins only when they need to do admin work, for a limited time. Which tool fits?

  • AAccess reviews of group membership
  • BSelf-service password reset for users
  • CPrivileged Identity Management
  • DAzure Bastion for remote desktop sessions
Show the answer

Answer: C. PIM gives just-in-time, time-bound privileged access.

S2Each quarter, managers must confirm that group members still need access. Which capability does this?

  • AAccess reviews
  • BID Protection
  • CSmart lockout
  • DFederation
Show the answer

Answer: A. Access reviews periodically confirm or remove access.

S3A sign-in comes from an anonymous IP address and an unusual location. Which tool classifies this as risky?

  • AAzure Firewall for network filtering
  • BMicrosoft Purview for data compliance
  • CMicrosoft Entra ID Protection
  • DAzure Key Vault for secrets and keys
Show the answer

Answer: C. ID Protection detects risky sign-ins and users.

S4A user's credentials appear in a leaked list. Which risk type is this?

  • AUser risk
  • BSign-in risk
  • CDevice risk
  • DNetwork risk
Show the answer

Answer: A. Leaked credentials indicate that the account may be compromised, which is user risk.

S5In PIM, what does "eligible" mean?

  • AThe user has the role permanently and can never lose it
  • BThe user can activate the role when needed
  • CThe user is blocked from the role until an admin approves
  • DThe role is deleted from the directory for everyone
Show the answer

Answer: B. Eligible users must activate the role before using it.

S6New employees, movers and leavers should get and lose access automatically as part of their life cycle. Which capability fits?

  • ALifecycle workflows in ID Governance
  • BConditional Access report-only mode for testing
  • CManaged identity for an Azure resource
  • DPassword protection with banned password lists
Show the answer

Answer: A. Lifecycle workflows automate joiner, mover and leaver tasks.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What does ID Governance manage?

Show the answer

The identity and access life cycle: the right access for the right people for the right time.

R2What can an access review check?

Show the answer

Group memberships, application access, roles and access packages.

R3What does PIM stand for?

Show the answer

Privileged Identity Management.

R4What is the difference between eligible and active in PIM?

Show the answer

Eligible can activate the role; active has it now.

R5Name the two risk types in ID Protection.

Show the answer

User risk and sign-in risk.

R6Which license level do PIM and ID Protection need?

Show the answer

Microsoft Entra ID P2 (or ID Governance for PIM).

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
ID Governance entitlement management (access packages), lifecycle workflows (joiner, mover, leaver), access reviews, PIM, terms of use
Access reviews periodic; reviewers owners, managers, users; approve or deny; auto-remove access
PIM just-in-time, time-bound, eligible vs active, approval, MFA on activation, audit; P2
ID Protection detects user risk (leaked credentials) and sign-in risk (impossible travel, anonymous IP); risk-based Conditional Access; P2
